aid.title: Harvey Mudd - Applying for Financial Aid

iaid.title: Harvey Mudd - International Student Financial Aid

test_policy.notes: Test-optional for fall 2027 applicants; HMC will return to requiring standardized testing for the fall 2028 cycle. Merit scholarships do not use test scores.

requirements.notes: Two supplemental essays (500 and 250 words) plus the personal essay. School Report from the counselor is required (the separate counselor recommendation is optional when available). Two teacher recommendations: one STEM teacher and one humanities/social science/arts teacher. Interview is optional. CSS Profile is required for need-based institutional aid. Common App document cutoffs: Jan 21 (ED II) and Feb 6 (RD).

deadlines.label: Early Decision I
deadlines.notes: Reply due Jan 8; optional interview by Nov 15.

deadlines.label: Early Decision II
deadlines.notes: Reply due Feb 26; optional interview by Dec 15.

deadlines.label: Regular Decision
deadlines.notes: Reply due May 1; optional interview by Dec 15.

deadlines.label: Merit scholarship deadline
deadlines.notes: Feb 1 for ED I, ED II and RD.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Waived if the school's primary language of instruction is English; the waiver is granted only after the application is submitted. Scores can be self-reported; only enrolling students must submit official reports.

english.notes: iBT Home Edition or iBT Paper Edition; the page does not mention the new 1-6 scale.
C1 Advanced min 190; C2 Proficiency min 200.

aid.notes: Aid goes to a small number of admitted international applicants; financial need may affect admission chances. HMC states it can meet 100% of demonstrated need for only a handful of international students. Students who enter without aid are not considered for aid later. Merit: the So International Scholarship (one recipient per entering class, offered regardless of need, no separate application); international students may also apply for some merit awards.

tier_notes.computer_science: One of the strongest undergraduate-only CS programs; not research-ranked.
tier_notes.engineering: Top undergraduate-only engineering program (general engineering B.S.).
tier_notes.math_physics: Mathematics and physics are exceptionally strong for an undergraduate-only college.
tier_notes.economics: No economics major (taken at other Claremont Colleges).
tier_notes.humanities: No humanities major, although one third of coursework is in humanities, social sciences and arts.
